Ealing is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable full bathroom installation and fitting services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Ealing and the surrounding Greater London region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional bathroom installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Greater London, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any full bathroom installation and fitting requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Ealing with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a new bathroom?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Replacing like-for-like or fitting a new bathroom within existing walls does not require planning permission. Moving soil stacks or creating a new bathroom in unconverted space may require Building Regulations approval.

faqs.q: Can you move the toilet and bath to different positions?
faqs.a: Yes, but it depends on the soil pipe route and floor structure. Moving a toilet more than a metre from the existing soil stack requires a new soil pipe connection and increases cost significantly.

faqs.q: How much does a bathroom installation cost?
faqs.a: Labour for a full bathroom installation typically ranges from £2,500 to £5,000 depending on complexity. Suite and tile costs are separate. A complete bathroom renovation including all materials typically costs £4,000 to £10,000+.

faqs.q: Should I supply my own bathroom suite or let the plumber supply it?
faqs.a: You can do either. Supplying your own suite gives you more choice and control over the brand and style. Your installer may offer trade discounts worth 15-30% off RRP if they supply.

localParagraph: Ealing is one of west London's most characterful boroughs, encompassing everything from the grand Edwardian semis of Pitshanger Lane and the Victorian terraces of Hanwell to modern apartment developments near Ealing Broadway station. This mix of housing eras means bathroom installation work here varies considerably — older properties often require full pipework updates, while newer builds may simply need a well-planned suite replacement. Water hardness across the borough sits in a mixed range, with some areas experiencing moderately hard supplies that can gradually affect shower heads, taps, and heating elements over time; a qualified installer working in Ealing will typically advise on appropriate limescale-resistant fittings or inline water softeners to extend the lifespan of a new bathroom. England's building regulations apply throughout, governing everything from ventilation requirements to electrical zones around wet areas, so homeowners should always ensure their installer is fully certified and able to sign off the work correctly. Getting the specification right from the outset saves considerable time and expense down the line.
whatItInvolves: A full bathroom installation covers everything from stripping out the existing suite to fitting the new one — including all pipework, waste connections, tiling preparation, flooring, and electrical work for lighting and extraction. A quality bathroom installation transforms one of the most-used rooms in your home and typically adds 3-5% to your property value.
process: The process starts with a detailed survey to assess existing pipework, drainage routes, and structural considerations. Day 1-2: strip out and prep. Day 3-4: first fix plumbing and any structural work. Day 5-7: suite installation, tiling, and second fix. Day 8-10: finishing, sealant, and final inspection. You'll be without a working bathroom for 5-10 days depending on complexity — we'll agree a realistic timeline upfront.
whatToExpect: Expect a detailed written quote covering labour, waste disposal, and any structural work. Suite and tiles are usually supplied separately by you or sourced through us. All plumbing work is carried out to Water Regulations standards. A bathroom installation is a major investment — ask to see previous work and Gas Safe registration before committing to any installer.
